narrative: The model estimates a 42% chance that you will fail your final year. This was the top factor and it pushed the prediction toward failing. The next most influential factor was your record of past class failures. You have none, matching the average for students who passed, and this worked in your favour by pushing toward passing. The third factor was your home-to-school travel time. Your trip of 30–60 minutes is longer than most passing students experience—only about five percent travel that long—but in your case it was treated as a modest point toward passing. Even with those positive signals, the model still sees enough risk to require support. To improve your position, make clear academic goals, especially whether you want to continue studying after school. Keep attendance steady, use the family support and internet access you have, and speak with your teachers about a study plan. The remedial courses are meant to give you that structure now.
